turns.text: A price alert. Where do I do that?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most flight search sites have a button for it. You'll get an email when the fare for your route drops.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, setting one up / for Toronto right now.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good luck. If it drops to a price you're happy with, just book it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're flying with our eighteen month old. Do we need to bring the car seat?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You don't have to, but it's often worth it, both for the flight if she has her own seat, and for taxis or rental cars at the other end.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She'll be on my lap, we didn't buy her a seat.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then you can usually check the car seat for free at the gate. Put it in a padded bag to protect it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Free? That's a relief.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most airlines don't charge for car seats or strollers. Check yours to be sure.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Any tips for keeping her / you know, not screaming the whole time?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Feed her or give her a dummy during takeoff and landing to help her ears. Pack new little toys she hasn't seen yet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: New toys. Smart.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: And snacks, lots of snacks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I have three days in Rome. Help me not waste them.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Three days is good. I'd group things by area so you're not crossing the city all the time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, how?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Day one, the Colosseum and the Forum. Day two, the Vatican museums and Saint Peter's. Day three, wander the center, Trevi Fountain and the Pantheon.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do I need to book things?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, book the Colosseum and the Vatican ahead online. The queues without tickets can be hours long.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hours. Wow. And I want / one really good dinner somewhere.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try Trastevere in the evening. Walk the side streets and pick a place where you hear more Italian than English.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I use my phone abroad without paying a fortune?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The cheapest option is usually a local or travel eSIM. You buy a data plan online and install it before you leave.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's an eSIM? Is it a physical thing?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No, it's digital. Your phone downloads it, like an app, as long as your phone supports it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I check that?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Look in your settings under mobile data or cellular. If there's an option to add an eSIM, you're good.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And my normal number / still works for texts?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, you can keep your normal SIM active for calls and texts. Just turn off its data roaming so you're not charged.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're taking a ferry to the islands and I get seasick on basically anything.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sit in the middle of the boat on a lower deck, where there's the least movement, and look at the horizon.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Not inside reading?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Definitely not reading. That's one of the worst things for seasickness.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about pills?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Motion sickness tablets work well for many people. Take them before you get on, not after you start feeling sick.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They make me drowsy though / is there anything else?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some people find ginger sweets or wristbands helpful. Fresh air on deck helps too, if it's not too rough.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm a woman traveling alone for the first time, to Portugal. My mum is very worried.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's natural for her. Portugal is generally considered quite safe, and lots of women travel there solo.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Any actual tips, though? Beyond be careful.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Share your plans with someone at home, and arrive in a new city during daylight if you can.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's useful.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Stay somewhere with good reviews from other solo women. And keep a little cash and a copy of your passport separate from your wallet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I was thinking of hostels / to meet people.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good idea. Many have female only dorms, and the common rooms are great for finding company for day trips.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'll show this to my mum.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: I hope it reassures her. Have a wonderful trip.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm forty-five and I've never stayed in a hostel. Am I too old?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not at all. Plenty of hostels have guests of every age, and many have private rooms too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A private room in a hostel? Then what's the point?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's usually cheaper than a hotel, and you still get the social side, like the kitchen, the bar and organized walks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm. I do like meeting people.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then look for hostels described as relaxed or social, not party hostels. Reviews tell you a lot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do I need to bring / my own towel and stuff?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sometimes. Many charge a small fee for towels, so a light travel towel is handy. A padlock for the lockers is useful too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My flight lands in Madrid at half past eleven at night. Taxi or train into the city?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: At that hour, a taxi is probably easiest. Madrid has a fixed taxi fare from the airport to the center.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, fixed? So no surprises.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. Just use the official taxi rank outside arrivals.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Would the metro still be running?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It usually runs until about half past one, but with luggage and a late arrival, it's more hassle.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right. I'll be tired and / probably grumpy, honestly.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then the taxi is worth it. You'll be at your hotel in about half an hour.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I take daily medication. What do I need to know for flying abroad?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Always pack it in your hand luggage, in its original packaging with the label on.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Not my suitcase?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No, bags get delayed. You don't want to land without your medication for two days.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do I need a letter from my doctor?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's a good idea, especially for injections or controlled medicines. Some countries have strict rules, so check the embassy website of where you're going.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And how much should I bring? It's a two week trip / I was thinking exactly two weeks.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bring a few extra days' worth, in case of delays. Splitting it between two bags is smart too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good idea. I'll ask my pharmacist for a bit extra.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect. And set reminders for the time difference, so you don't miss a dose.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My sister and I are going to the Christmas markets in Germany. What do I wear? I'm from Florida.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Layers, lots of them. It can be around freezing, and you'll be standing outside for hours.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Freezing. Okay. I own exactly one coat.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Make sure it's warm and ideally waterproof. Add thermal underwear, a thick jumper, a hat, a scarf and gloves.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Thermal underwear. Very glamorous.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's the secret of every happy market visitor. Good boots with thick socks matter too, cold feet ruin everything.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the mulled wine / keeps you warm, right?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It helps your hands at least. You often pay a deposit for the mug, and you can keep it as a souvenir.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I have about sixty thousand air miles. Is it smarter to use them for flights or upgrades?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Usually, long haul business class upgrades or reward seats give the most value per mile.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about short flights?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Short flights often give poor value, since cash fares are cheap and taxes on rewards can be high.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My partner wants to use them for a hotel.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hotels are usually one of the worst uses of airline miles. I'd save them for a flight.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We were looking at New York in spring. Could I / get two economy tickets with that?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Quite possibly, depending on where you're flying from and the airline. Check the reward chart and book early, reward seats sell out.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What are my chances of seeing the northern lights in Iceland in late February?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Late February is actually a decent time. The nights are still long, and the season runs roughly from September to April.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do I need a tour?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not necessarily, but tours know where the skies are clear. If you rent a car, check the aurora forecast and cloud cover each evening.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is there an app or something?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, the Icelandic weather office has an aurora forecast online, and there are several apps.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And if it's cloudy all week? / I'll be so sad.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It can happen, so plan other things too, like hot springs and waterfalls. Staying four or five nights gives you more chances.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Five nights then.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good choice. Pack warm, the waiting outside can get chilly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My teenagers hate sightseeing. How do I plan a city trip they won't sulk through?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Let each of them choose one thing for the trip. Ownership makes a huge difference with teens.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One of them will choose a shopping mall.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's okay. Balance it with activities that don't feel like sightseeing, like bike tours, food markets or a climbing park.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Food markets might work. They're always hungry.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect, use that. A street food tour can feel more like an adventure than a museum.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And mornings? They / sleep until noon on holiday.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Let them. Plan the big activity for the afternoon and keep mornings for things you and your partner want to do.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm visiting the States for the first time. The tipping thing confuses me. Who do I tip?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: In restaurants with table service, around fifteen to twenty percent of the bill is normal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Twenty percent? On top of the price?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, and tax is often added at the till too, so the menu price isn't what you'll pay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, that's a shock. What about taxis?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Roughly fifteen percent for taxis and rideshares. Hotel staff who carry bags usually get a couple of dollars per bag.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And coffee shops? There's always / that little tip screen.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's optional for counter service. Tip if you want to, but nobody expects it the way restaurants do.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My flight got overbooked and they want volunteers to take a later one. Should I do it?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It depends on your plans. If you're flexible, you can often get a voucher or cash for it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What should I ask for?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask what the compensation is, when the new flight leaves, and whether they'll cover meals or a hotel if it's the next day.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I negotiate?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sometimes. If nobody volunteers, the offer often goes up, so you don't have to accept the first one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It's only a four hour wait / so I'm tempted.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then it could be a good deal. Make sure your new seat is confirmed before you give up your current one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Smart. Going to the desk now.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good luck. Ask for a lounge pass too while you're there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We want to go to the Edinburgh festival in August. When should we book somewhere to stay?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: As soon as possible. Accommodation fills up months ahead and prices climb a lot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It's January now. Is that already late?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not too late, but don't wait much longer. Look at places with free cancellation so you can lock something in now.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Could we stay outside the city?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, towns along the train line can be much cheaper. Check the last train times though, shows run late.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good point. We'll want / to see some of the late night comedy.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then staying central is worth the money, or plan on taxis back.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How much should I budget per day in Mexico City? I'm a student, so, not much.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You can do it fairly cheaply. A hostel bed, street food and the metro keep costs very low.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Like how low?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Many backpackers spend somewhere around thirty to forty dollars a day, but prices change, so check recent travel forums.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is street food safe?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Busy stalls with lots of locals are usually a good sign. Avoid tap water and ice from places you're unsure about.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's the one thing / I shouldn't skip?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A day at Teotihuacan, the ancient pyramids just outside the city. Get there early to beat the heat and the crowds.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Pyramids. Okay, adding it.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: And try the tacos al pastor. They're worth the trip on their own.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Vienna to Venice. Night train or a quick flight?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The night train saves you a hotel night and drops you in the city center. The flight is faster but you'd still need to get from the airport.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do night trains have proper beds?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, you can book a sleeper cabin with beds, or a cheaper couchette that you share.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Shared with strangers? Hmm.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Couchettes can be fine, but if you want privacy, a private sleeper is worth it. Book early, they're popular.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, private. And I arrive / around breakfast time, right?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Usually in the morning, yes. Arriving in Venice by train and walking straight out onto the Grand Canal is a lovely way to start.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hello. My grandson usually books things for me, but he's away. I'd like to book a train to visit my sister.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Of course, I can help. Do you know which station you're traveling from and to, and the day?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: From the main station here to Bath, on Thursday.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lovely. The simplest way is the train company's website, or you could buy a ticket at the station counter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The website frightens me a little, to be honest.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's perfectly fine. Buying at the counter is easy, and the staff can find you the best price. Mention if you have a senior railcard.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I believe I do. It's / somewhere in my handbag.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bring it along, it can save you about a third. And ask for a seat reservation so you have a guaranteed seat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Thank you, dear. That's very helpful.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You're welcome. Enjoy your visit with your sister.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What do I do with leftover foreign coins? I've got a jar full from about six countries.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Banks and exchange offices rarely take coins, only notes. So the options are a bit limited.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So they're useless?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not quite. Many airlines and airports have charity collection boxes that take any currency.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's nice actually.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It is. Or keep them for your next trip to those countries, or give them to a kid who collects coins.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My nephew might like that / he's into maps right now.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect. He could match each coin to its country on a map.

option_sets.lead_in: We're trying to pick where to go for a long weekend in the spring.
options: The first option is a beach town about four hours away, warm, but it might still be a little too cold to swim.
Then there's a big city trip with museums and restaurants, but the hotels there are pretty expensive.
Option three is a cabin in the mountains, really quiet, with hiking trails right outside the door.
And the last one is just staying home and doing day trips, which would save a lot of money.
moshi_comment: If you want to recharge, the mountain cabin sounds perfect, quiet and close to nature. The city trip is great for food and culture, but those hotel prices could add up fast. The beach town might be a bit disappointing if it's too cold to swim.

What are you hoping to get out of the weekend, rest or excitement? For rest, I'd pick the cabin. For excitement, the city is the clear winner, and day trips from home are a nice backup if money is tight.

option_sets.lead_in: My sister and I can't agree on how to get to the wedding next month.
options: One way is to fly, which takes about two hours, but the tickets are expensive this close to the date.
Another is to take the train, around seven hours, but it's comfortable and we can work on the way.
Or we could drive, which is cheapest split between two people, though it's a long day in the car.
moshi_comment: The train sounds like a nice middle ground, it's comfortable and you don't lose the whole day since you can work. Flying is fastest, but those last minute prices hurt. Driving is cheapest, and you'd have a car once you get there, which can be handy.
Will you need a car at the wedding location? If yes, driving together probably makes the most sense. If not, I'd take the train, it's much more relaxing than seven hours behind the wheel.

option_sets.lead_in: We want a ski trip in February but none of us are great skiers. I found three places.
options: There's a big famous resort with tons of slopes, lively nightlife, and prices to match.
A small family resort in the next valley, cheaper and quieter, with mostly gentle beginner runs.
Or a ski school package, where lessons, boots and lift passes are all included in one price.
moshi_comment: For a group of not great skiers, the small family resort makes a lot of sense, you'd use most of the slopes. The big resort is fun, but you'd pay for runs you won't ski. The package is the safest if anyone is a real beginner.

I'd look hard at the package, lessons make the week far more fun when you're still learning. If some of you are confident already, the small resort plus a couple of lessons could be cheaper. The famous resort is better saved for when you've improved.

option_sets.lead_in: I've got a ten hour layover in Istanbul and I'm not sure what to do with it.
options: I could stay in the airport lounge, shower, nap and eat, nice and stress free.
Or take the metro into the old city, see a mosque or two and get back in time, hopefully.
There's also a short guided tour the airline offers for transit passengers, about six hours with a guide.
moshi_comment: Ten hours is enough to leave the airport, so I'd go for the airline tour, it handles the timing and the visa questions for you. Going alone is fine too if you're confident, just leave plenty of buffer. The lounge is good if you're exhausted.

If you've never seen the city, the guided tour gives you a taste without the risk of missing your flight. Doing it alone gives more freedom but you'd have to watch the clock. The lounge is a sensible fallback if you're tired.

option_sets.lead_in: Summer holiday with three kids under ten, and my husband and I want different things.
options: He wants a theme park resort in Florida, which the kids would adore but it's crazy expensive.
I'd love a lake cabin up north where they swim, catch frogs and go to bed early.
My mum suggested we stay with her in the city and do day trips to the zoo and the beach.
Or a camping style holiday park with pools and kids' clubs, somewhere in between.
moshi_comment: The holiday park might be the sweet spot, it has the fun the kids would get in Florida for much less money, and you still get some quiet. The lake cabin is lovely but might feel slow for him. Your mum's offer is the cheapest and a nice bonus for her.

Florida would be magical for that age but it's a lot of money and queues. The lake cabin and your mum's place are both relaxed and cheaper. If you need a compromise, the holiday park splits the difference.

option_sets.lead_in: I'm taking a gap year after school and I've narrowed it down to a few plans.
options: Working at a ski lodge in Canada for the winter, then traveling with the money I've saved.
Volunteering on an organic farm in New Zealand, which gives me free food and a bed.
Teaching English in South Korea, with a proper salary but a one year contract.
Interrailing around Europe, which would be amazing, but I'd need to save for months first.
moshi_comment: Teaching in Korea gives you real savings and work experience, but a year contract is a big commitment. The ski lodge is a classic, fun and flexible. The farm is cheap and relaxing. Interrailing is great, maybe as the final trip after one of the others.

You could chain two of them, like the ski lodge for the winter and then interrailing with what you earn. The farm in New Zealand is good if you want calm. Korea is the most serious choice, best if you're curious about teaching.
